newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian Utenos has agreement with investor.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian Utenos has agreement with investor.

text.p: A leading Lithuanian brewer, Utenos Beverages, courted by Carlsberg and Finnish-Norwegian Baltic Beverage Holdings (BBH), said on Wednesday it has signed a letter of intent with an investor.
The company refused to name the investor.
Newspaper Verslo Zinios earlier said that BBH wanted to buy 50 percent or less of Utenos. BBH, owned by Finnish Hartwall and Norwegian Orkla, already owns another leading brewer, Kalnapilis.
Board chairman Arunas Lubys confirmed the report.
"We received a BBH offer in April and discussed it in the board meeting but we cannot carry out two parallel investment projects," Lubys told Reuters.
"We signed earlier a letter of intent with another investor, so we have no right to pursue talks with BBH while this protocol of intent is valid," Lubys said.
Lubys declined to name which investor Utenos signed the letter of intent with.
Carlsberg earlier confirmed that it has had contacts with Utenos but would not comment further.
Lubys said that Utenos had received no further suggestions from BBH and a price of 300 litas per share mentioned in the paper news to him.
"There were no talks about the share price with any investor," Lubys said.
"All the investors want a controling package of shares in Utenos," Lubys added.
He also said that Utenos' share of the beer market decreased to 24 percent from 35 percent last year.
"We will try to regain our share of the market, but around 60 million litas to 80 million litas of investments into production and marketing would be necessary," Lubys said.

He noted that the company cannot sell shares at the moment as it has failed to register a new issue with the securities commission over a disagreement with the government, which owns 21.5 percent of Utenos.
